# A rebuilt pane loses its FLIP marker, so recreate never animates

## Context

A pane rebuilt by the engine's reload/recreate transaction is missing its FLIP marker, so it is excluded from dock motion for the rest of its life. Found while covering the reload action in a downstream consumer, where the missing marker also caused me to misdiagnose a working recreate as pane destruction — that misdiagnosis is the second, cheaper reason this matters: the marker is the obvious witness for "which pane is this", and its absence on one path misleads consumers and their tests, not just the animation.

Verified empirically before filing, on a real consumer with `Neo.config.useSharedWorkers`, by clicking the header's reload action on a focused pane:

```
before   flip-marked panes: 3   app widgets: 3   pane id: …connection-info-1
after    flip-marked panes: 2   app widgets: 3   pane id: …connection-info-2
```

The recreate itself is correct — a fresh instance replaced the live one in the same slot, siblings intact, zero console errors. Only the marker is gone.

## The Problem

`decorateFlipMarker(config, itemId)` stamps `dock-flip-item-<itemId>` onto a pane config so the `DockFlip` main-thread addon can identify that pane across a re-projection and animate it from its old box to its new one. Three code paths produce a pane candidate. Two decorate; one does not.

The consequence is silent and permanent for that instance: nothing throws, nothing logs, the pane renders and works. It simply stops participating in motion, so the next layout change snaps it into place while its siblings animate. A user sees an inconsistent dock; a consumer keying on the marker (CSS, an e2e locator, a debug overlay) sees the pane vanish.

Note this is reachable by default now. `hasDockRecreateFallback()` answers a constant `true` because the base `resolveFreshPane` delegates to `resolvePane`, so every consumer that returns a config from `resolvePane` — the documented normal case — gets a live reload action and therefore this path.

## The Architectural Reality

| path | producer | decorated |
|---|---|---|
| projection | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2616` — `this.decorateFlipMarker(this.resolvePane(itemId, item), itemId)` | ✅ |
| rail reveal | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2314` — `resolveRevealComponentRef: (…) => me.decorateFlipMarker(me.resolveRevealPane(itemId, item), itemId)` | ✅ |
| **recreate** | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` — `prepareRecreateCandidate` calls `this.resolveFreshPane(itemId, item)` **raw** | ❌ |

`decorateFlipMarker` is defined at `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1098`. The base `resolveFreshPane` (`:2655`) returns `this.resolvePane(itemId, item)` — the *undecorated* resolver, not the decorated wrapper at `:2616` — which is the precise point at which the marker is lost.

Phase 2 (`commitRecreateCandidate`) then inserts the candidate through `container.insert(index, candidate)`, so whatever the candidate carries is what the live slot gets. The transaction is otherwise sound: insert-then-remove with `destroy: false`, so no window exists in which the slot is empty.

## The Fix

Decorate at the recreate site, in `prepareRecreateCandidate`:

```js
candidate = this.decorateFlipMarker(this.resolveFreshPane(itemId, item), itemId)
```

Chosen over fixing the base `resolveFreshPane` to delegate to the decorated wrapper, because a consumer that **overrides** `resolveFreshPane` (the documented extension point for a cache-backed factory) would still return an undecorated candidate and re-open the same gap. Decorating what the hook returns covers the base and every override with one line.

`decorateFlipMarker` must remain tolerant of a non-config candidate: a consumer may legitimately return a live component instance from `resolveFreshPane`, and phase 1's own `live-instance` guard only rejects the *predecessor* instance, not any instance. Confirm its current behaviour on an instance input before changing the call site.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dock-flip-item-<itemId>` class on a pane | `Workspace#decorateFlipMarker` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1098`) | present on every projected pane **including** one produced by recreate | unchanged for the two paths that already decorate | `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts.md` describes FLIP motion; no doc change needed | measured 3 → 2 marked panes across one reload while widget count held at 3 |
| `Workspace#resolveFreshPane` | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2655` | contract unchanged — consumers keep returning a config or an instance | override-safe: the caller decorates, not the hook | JSDoc on the member | base delegates to `resolvePane`, verified at `:2655` |

| `Workspace#prepareRecreateCandidate` | Existing `decorateFlipMarker` and projection semantics | Plain-config candidates return a decorated shallow copy preserving supplied values; component candidates preserve identity and predecessor-instance refusal | Existing `threw`, `declined`, and `live-instance` outcomes unchanged | Method/helper JSDoc | Distinct-candidate and five FLIP arms |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — the docking record's FLIP-motion and recreate clauses both stand; this is an implementation gap against them, not a change to either. No ADR amendment required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `prepareRecreateCandidate` decorates the candidate returned by `resolveFreshPane`, so a recreated pane carries `dock-flip-item-<itemId>`.
- [ ] A red-first unit arm proves the gap before the fix: a workspace whose `resolvePane` returns a plain config, recreated, asserts the marker present — failing on current `dev`.
- [ ] A consumer that **overrides** `resolveFreshPane` also receives a decorated candidate (the override case is the reason for the chosen call site, so it needs its own arm).
- [ ] `decorateFlipMarker`'s behaviour on a live-component candidate is asserted, so the tolerant path is a contract rather than an accident.
- [ ] No change to the two paths that already decorate, and no double-stamping when a candidate already carries the marker.
- [ ] Existing dock unit + component tiers stay green.

## Out of Scope

- The recreate transaction's structure. Insert-then-remove with `destroy: false` is correct and is not touched.
- Whether reload should be enabled by default. `hasDockRecreateFallback()` returning a constant `true` is deliberate per its own JSDoc and is a separate question.
- Any consumer-side workaround. Three candidate paths with one rule between them is exactly the shape that must not be re-derived per consumer.
- FLIP motion behaviour itself — this restores a pane's eligibility for it, it does not change the animation.

## Avoided Traps

- **Fixing it in the consumer.** The tempting one-liner is for the app's `resolveFreshPane` to stamp the marker itself. That is how a single engine rule becomes three consumer re-derivations; the same class of mistake as the drop-preview positioning that three consumers each re-derived before `#18142` moved it into the engine.
- **Fixing the base `resolveFreshPane` instead of the call site.** Reads cleaner and silently excludes every consumer override, which is the documented extension point.
- **Asserting the marker in a downstream consumer's e2e tier.** An arm that reds until an engine bump lands makes that tier untrustworthy for the whole interval; the witness belongs here, next to the code.

## Related

- `#18142` — the drop-preview geometry that three consumers each re-derived before the engine absorbed it; same anti-pattern, cited as precedent for where this fix belongs.
- `#18283` — the reload journey witnessing engine recreate for a pane without the delegation contract; that arm passes without noticing the marker, which is how this survived.
- Epics #18303 / #18304 — the ownership arc this path sits inside.
